questions.question_text:
Statements: A ≥ B > C = D; E ≥ D < F > U
Conclusions: I. E > B; II. F ≥ C
Which conclusion(s) follow?

options.B: Either conclusion I or II is true
options.C: Both conclusions I and II are true
options.D: Only conclusion II is true
options.E: Neither conclusion I nor II is true

questions.explanation: Since D=C and B>C, E≥D does not establish E>B. But F>D=C gives F>C, so only conclusion II follows.

questions.question_text:
Statements: S > B = Y ≤ U; T > Y < F ≤ P
Conclusions: I. P > B; II. S > Y
Which conclusion(s) follow?

options.B: Either conclusion I or II is true
options.C: Both conclusions I and II are true
options.D: Only conclusion II is true
options.E: Neither conclusion I nor II is true

questions.explanation: B=Y and P≥F>Y, so P>B. Also S>B=Y, so both conclusions follow.

questions.question_text:
Statements: D ≥ E < S; P ≤ Y ≤ E
Conclusions: I. D > Y; II. P = D
Which conclusion(s) follow?

options.C: Either conclusion I or II is true
options.D: Both conclusions I and II are true
options.E: Neither conclusion I nor II is true

questions.explanation: The chain gives D≥E≥Y, which does not guarantee the strict relation D>Y. P≤Y≤E≤D also does not force P=D. Neither conclusion is certain.

questions.question_text:
Statements: E < H > P; H < O < N
Conclusions: I. P < E; II. E > N
Which conclusion(s) follow?

options.C: Either conclusion I or II is true
options.D: Both conclusions I and II are true
options.E: Neither conclusion I nor II is true

questions.explanation: E and P are both below H, but their order is unknown. The other chain gives E<H<O<N, so E>N is contradicted. Neither conclusion follows.

questions.question_text:
Statements: D ≥ E < S; P ≤ Y ≤ E
Conclusions: I. P < S; II. D ≥ Y
Which conclusion(s) follow?

options.C: Either conclusion I or II is true
options.D: Both conclusions I and II are true
options.E: Neither conclusion I nor II is true

questions.explanation: P≤Y≤E<S proves P<S. D≥E≥Y proves D≥Y. Both conclusions follow.

questions.question_text:
Statements: R < Q = W ≤ B; B > T = M < U
Conclusions: I. W < M; II. M > Q
Which conclusion(s) follow?

options.C: Either conclusion I or II is true
options.D: Both conclusions I and II are true
options.E: Neither conclusion I nor II is true

questions.explanation: Q=W≤B and B>M, but W may be below, equal to, or above M. There is no definite relation between M and Q=W. Neither conclusion follows.

questions.question_text:
Statements: L = T ≤ R = S; R ≤ Q = V ≥ A
Conclusions: I. L ≤ V; II. A = L
Which conclusion(s) follow?

options.C: Either conclusion I or II is true
options.D: Both conclusions I and II are true
options.E: Neither conclusion I nor II is true

questions.explanation: L=T≤R≤Q=V establishes L≤V. A and L are both at most V but are otherwise unrelated, so A=L is not certain.

questions.question_text:
Statements: S > U < P ≤ E = A; W ≤ K ≤ U
Conclusions: I. W ≤ P; II. A ≥ W
Which conclusion(s) follow?

options.C: Either conclusion I or II is true
options.D: Both conclusions I and II are true
options.E: Neither conclusion I nor II is true

questions.explanation:
W≤K≤U

U≥W, so A>W. Both conclusions follow.

questions.question_text:
Statements: B ≤ F < A ≤ T ≥ R; X ≥ A > Z
Conclusions: I. X > F; II. T > B
Which conclusion(s) follow?

options.C: Either conclusion I or II is true
options.D: Both conclusions I and II are true
options.E: Neither conclusion I nor II is true

questions.explanation: X≥A>F proves X>F. Also T≥A>F≥B proves T>B. Both conclusions follow.

questions.question_text:
Statements: A ≤ Q = K < G ≥ Y = O; W > U ≥ Q
Conclusions: I. W > K; II. O ≤ G
Which conclusion(s) follow?

options.C: Either conclusion I or II is true
options.D: Both conclusions I and II are true
options.E: Neither conclusion I nor II is true

questions.explanation: W>U≥Q=K proves W>K. O=Y≤G is given, so both conclusions follow.

questions.question_text:
Statements: D = X < J > K ≥ Q; S ≤ E ≤ D ≤ R
Conclusions: I. S < J; II. R ≥ K
Which conclusion(s) follow?

options.C: Either conclusion I or II is true
options.D: Both conclusions I and II are true
options.E: Neither conclusion I nor II is true

questions.explanation: S≤E≤D=X<J proves S<J. The statements do not relate D (or R) to K, so R≥K is not certain. Only conclusion I follows.

questions.question_text:
Statements: O ≥ C = P > U = Z; N < E ≤ C > R
Conclusions: I. R < O; II. O ≥ Z
Which conclusion(s) follow?

options.C: Either conclusion I or II is true
options.D: Both conclusions I and II are true
options.E: Neither conclusion I nor II is true

questions.explanation: R<C≤O proves R<O. Also O≥C=P>U=Z proves O>Z, hence O≥Z. Both conclusions follow.

questions.question_text:
Statements: M < U < T < K ≤ B < H; K > N ≥ Y
Conclusions: I. M < Y; II. T ≥ N
Which conclusion(s) follow?

options.C: Either conclusion I or II is true
options.D: Both conclusions I and II are true
options.E: Neither conclusion I nor II is true

questions.explanation: M and Y are both below K, with no stated order between them. T and N are also both below K, with no stated order. Neither conclusion is guaranteed.

questions.question_text:
Statements: F > R ≥ D > M ≤ V < L; M > G > Q
Conclusions: I. R > Q; II. L < G
Which conclusion(s) follow?

options.C: Either conclusion I or II is true
options.D: Both conclusions I and II are true
options.E: Neither conclusion I nor II is true

questions.explanation: R≥D>M>G>Q gives R>Q. M≤V<L and M>G imply L>M>G, contradicting L<G. Only conclusion I follows.

questions.question_text:
Statements: G ≤ Y < D < I; O > P > C > B = I
Conclusions: I. Y > O; II. B > G
Which conclusion(s) follow?

options.C: Either conclusion I or II is true
options.D: Both conclusions I and II are true
options.E: Neither conclusion I nor II is true

questions.explanation: The chains give G≤Y<D<I=B<C<P<O, so Y<O (not Y>O) while B>G. Only conclusion II follows.

questions.question_text:
Statements: A > T > M > R = S; T ≤ Q
Conclusions: I. Q > S; II. R < A
Which conclusion(s) follow?

options.C: Either conclusion I or II is true
options.D: Both conclusions I and II are true
options.E: Neither conclusion I nor II is true

questions.explanation: Q≥T>A>T>M>R=S establishes Q>S. A>T>M>R establishes R<A. Both conclusions follow.

questions.question_text:
Statements: A > B ≥ C ≥ D = E ≤ F = G ≤ H ≤ I < J ≥ K ≥ L = M > N
Conclusions: I. E ≤ B; II. B = E
Which conclusion(s) follow?

options.C: Either conclusion I or II is true
options.D: Neither conclusion I nor II is true
options.E: Both conclusions I and II are true

questions.explanation: B≥C≥D=E proves E≤B. The statements do not force equality B=E, so only conclusion I follows.

questions.question_text:
Statements: A > B ≥ C ≥ D = E ≤ F = G ≤ H ≤ I < J ≥ K ≥ L = M > N
Conclusions: I. I < E; II. E = I
Which conclusion(s) follow?

options.C: Either conclusion I or II is true
options.D: Neither conclusion I nor II is true
options.E: Both conclusions I and II are true

questions.explanation: The statement gives E≤I. It does not require equality: E<I is possible, and then I<E and E=I are both false. Neither conclusion follows.

questions.question_text:
Statements: A > B ≥ C ≥ D = E ≤ F = G ≤ H ≤ I < J ≥ K ≥ L = M > N
Conclusions: I. G < N; II. N ≥ G
Which conclusion(s) follow?

options.C: Either conclusion I or II is true
options.D: Neither conclusion I nor II is true
options.E: Both conclusions I and II are true

questions.explanation: G and N lie on separate branches below J; their relative order is not fixed. Assignments with G>N make both conclusions false, so neither follows.

questions.question_text:
Statements: A > B ≥ C ≥ D = E ≤ F = G ≤ H ≤ I < J ≥ K ≥ L = M > N
Conclusions: I. C ≥ L; II. L > C
Which conclusion(s) follow?

options.C: Either conclusion I or II is true
options.D: Neither conclusion I nor II is true
options.E: Both conclusions I and II are true

questions.explanation: The two conclusions are complementary: either C≥L or L>C, and exactly one holds for any values of C and L. Thus the either-or conclusion follows.

questions.question_text:
Statements: A > B ≥ C ≥ D = E ≤ F = G ≤ H ≤ I < J ≥ K ≥ L = M > N
Conclusions: I. E < H; II. E = H
Which conclusion(s) follow?

options.C: Either conclusion I or II is true
options.D: Neither conclusion I nor II is true
options.E: Both conclusions I and II are true

questions.explanation: E≤F=G≤H, so E is either strictly below H or equal to H. These mutually exclusive cases exhaust the possibilities; the either-or conclusion follows.

questions.question_text:
Statements: A > B ≥ C ≥ D = E ≤ F = G ≤ H ≤ I < J ≥ K ≥ L = M > N
Conclusions: I. D < F; II. E = G
Which conclusion(s) follow?

options.C: Either conclusion I or II is true
options.D: Both conclusions I and II are true
options.E: Neither conclusion I nor II is true

questions.explanation: D=E and F=G, with E≤F. If E<F, conclusion I (D<F) is true; if E=F, conclusion II (E=G) is true. These cases are mutually exclusive and exhaustive, so the either-or conclusion follows.

questions.question_text:
Statements: A > B ≥ C ≥ D = E ≤ F = G ≤ H ≤ I < J ≥ K ≥ L = M > N
Conclusions: I. C < O; II. C ≥ O
Which conclusion(s) follow?

options.C: Either conclusion I or II is true
options.D: Both conclusions I and II are true
options.E: Neither conclusion I nor II is true

questions.explanation: O is not related to the variables in the statement. For any C and O, exactly one of C<O or C≥O holds, so the either-or conclusion is true.

questions.question_text:
Statements: A > B ≥ C ≥ D = E ≤ F = G ≤ H ≤ I < J ≥ K ≥ L = M > N
Conclusions: I. J ≥ N; II. J < N
Which conclusion(s) follow?

options.C: Either conclusion I or II is true
options.D: Both conclusions I and II are true
options.E: Neither conclusion I nor II is true

questions.explanation: J>K≥L=M>N establishes J>N, hence J≥N. J<N is contradicted. Only conclusion I follows.

questions.question_text:
Statement: A > B ≥ C ≥ D = R ≤ H ≤ I < K ≥ L = M
Conclusions: I. C > L; II. L ≤ C
Which conclusion(s) follow?

options.C: Both conclusions 1 and 2 follow
options.D: Neither conclusion 1 nor 2 follows
options.E: Either conclusion 1 or 2 follows

questions.explanation: The statement does not order C and L. C>L implies L≤C, but equality also makes L≤C true while C>L is false; with C<L both conclusions are false. Neither conclusion is guaranteed.

questions.question_text:
Statement: A > B ≥ C ≥ D = R ≤ H ≤ I < K ≥ L = M
Conclusions: I. I ≤ D; II. I > D
Which conclusion(s) follow?

options.C: Both conclusions 1 and 2 follow
options.D: Neither conclusion 1 nor 2 follows
options.E: Either conclusion 1 or 2 follows

questions.explanation: D≤H≤I establishes I≥D. If I=D, conclusion I holds; if I>D, conclusion II holds. Exactly one follows in every permitted case.

questions.question_text: In which expression do both ‘Z ≥ X’ and ‘V > Y’ hold definitely?

options.C: Z ≥ Y = X ≤ W < V
options.D: Z ≥ Y < X ≤ W > V
options.E: None of the above

questions.explanation: In option C, Z≥Y=X gives Z≥X. Also V>W≥X=Y gives V>Y. The other expressions do not guarantee both requested relations.
